import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from datetime import datetime

# Connect to database
conn = sqlite3.connect('dacomp-092.sqlite')

# Get all columns
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(quickbooks__customer_analytics);")
columns = [col[1] for col in cursor.fetchall()]

# Initialize profiling results storage
profiling_results = {}

# Function to determine data type
def get_data_type(series):
    if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(series):
        if series.nunique() > 30:
            return 'numeric_continuous'
        return 'numeric_discrete'
    elif pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(series):
        return 'temporal'
    elif series.dtype == 'object':
        if series.nunique() < 20:
            return 'categorical_low_cardinality'
        return 'categorical_high_cardinality'
    elif pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(series):
        return 'boolean'
    return 'other'

# Function to profile numeric columns
def profile_numeric(series):
    profile = {
        'missing_values': series.isna().mean(),
        'unique_values': series.nunique(),
        'skewness': series.skew(),
        'kurtosis': series.kurtosis(),
        'iqr': series.quantile(0.75) - series.quantile(0.25),
        'iqr_outliers': (series < (series.quantile(0.25) - 1.5 * series.iqr())) | 
                        (series > (series.quantile(0.75) + 1.5 * series.iqr())),
        'zscore_outliers': np.abs((series - series.mean()) / series.std()) > 3,
        'isolation_forest': IsolationForest(contamination=0.05).fit(series.values.reshape(-1, 1)).predict(series.values.reshape(-1, 1)) == -1,
        'top_values': series.value_counts().head(20)
    }
    return profile

# Function to profile categorical columns
def profile_categorical(series):
    profile = {
        'missing_values': series.isna().mean(),
        'unique_values': series.nunique(),
        'top_values': series.value_counts().head(20)
    }
    return profile

# Main profiling function
def profile_column(column_name):
    query = f"SELECT {column_name} FROM quickbooks__customer_analytics"
    series = pd.read_sql(query, conn)[column_name]
    
    profile = {
        'data_type': get_data_type(series),
        'missing_values': series.isna().mean(),
        'unique_values': series.nunique()
    }
    
    if profile['data_type'] == 'numeric_continuous':
        profile.update(profile_numeric(series))
    elif profile['data_type'] in ['numeric_discrete', 'boolean']:
        profile.update(profile_numeric(series))
    elif profile['data_type'] in ['categorical_low_cardinality', 'categorical_high_cardinality']:
        profile.update(profile_categorical(series))
    
    profiling_results[column_name] = profile
    print(f"Profiled {column_name} ({profile['data_type']})")

# Profile all columns in batches
batch_size = 10
for i in range(0, len(columns), batch_size):
    batch = columns[i:i+batch_size]
    for col in batch:
        profile_column(col)
        print(f"Completed {i+len(batch)}/{len(columns)} columns")

# Save results to CSV
results_df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(profiling_results, orient='index')
results_df.to_csv('column_profiles.csv')
print("Profiling complete. Results saved to column_profiles.csv")

conn.close()

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load profiling results
results = pd.read_csv('column_profiles.csv', index_col=0)

# 1. Missing Value Analysis
missing_values = results['missing_values'].sort_values(ascending=False)
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.barplot(x=missing_values.values, y=missing_values.index)
plt.title('Missing Values by Column')
plt.xlabel('Missing Value Proportion')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('missing_values.png')
plt.close()

# 2. Data Type Distribution
type_counts = results['data_type'].value_counts()
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.barplot(x=type_counts.index, y=type_counts.values)
plt.title('Column Data Type Distribution')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.savefig('data_type_distribution.png')
plt.close()

# 3. Top Frequent Values (for categorical columns)
categorical_cols = results[results['data_type'].str.contains('categorical')]
top_values = pd.concat([results.loc[c, 'top_values'] for c in categorical_cols.index])
top_values = top_values.explode().value_counts().head(20)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x=top_values.values, y=top_values.index)
plt.title('Top 20 Most Frequent Values Across Categorical Columns')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('top_frequent_values.png')
plt.close()

# 4. Numeric Column Distributions (sample of 5 columns)
numeric_cols = results[results['data_type'].str.contains('numeric')]
sample_numeric = numeric_cols.sample(5).index

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
for i, col in enumerate(sample_numeric, 1):
    plt.subplot(2, 3, i)
    query = f"SELECT {col} FROM quickbooks__customer_analytics"
    data = pd.read_sql(query, conn)[col]
    sns.histplot(data.dropna(), kde=True)
    plt.title(col)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('numeric_distributions.png')
plt.close()

# Generate summary report
summary_stats = {
    'total_columns': len(results),
    'columns_with_missing_values': sum(results['missing_values'] > 0),
    'columns_with_outliers': sum(results['iqr_outliers'].notna()),
    'most_common_data_type': results['data_type'].mode()[0],
    'most_missing_column': results.loc[results['missing_values'].idxmax(), 'data_type']
}

with open('analysis_summary.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write("Data Profiling Summary Report\n")
    f.write("="*40 + "\n")
    f.write(f"Total Columns Analyzed: {summary_stats['total_columns']}\n")
    f.write(f"Columns with Missing Values: {summary_stats['columns_with_missing_values']}\n")
    f.write(f"Columns with Outliers Detected: {summary_stats['columns_with_missing_values']}\n")
    f.write(f"Most Common Data Type: {summary_stats['most_common_data_type']}\n")
    f.write(f"Column with Most Missing Values: {summary_stats['most_missing_column']}\n")
    f.write("\nVisualizations saved as:\n")
    f.write("- missing_values.png\n")
    f.write("- data_type_distribution.png\n")
    f.write("- top_frequent_values.png\n")
    f.write("- numeric_distributions.png\n")

conn.close()

import seaborn as sns
import ast
import sqlite3

# Load profiling results
results = pd.read_csv('column_profiles.csv', index_col=0)

# Function to safely parse top_values
def parse_top_values(top_values_str):
    try:
        if pd.isna(top_values_str):
            return pd.Series()
        return pd.Series(ast.literal_eval(top_values_str))
    except:
        return pd.Series()

# Re-establish database connection
conn = sqlite3.connect('dacomp-092.sqlite')

# 1. Missing Value Analysis
missing_values = results['missing_values'].sort_values(ascending=False)
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.barplot(x=missing_values.values, y=missing_values.index)
plt.title('Missing Values by Column')
plt.xlabel('Missing Value Proportion')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('missing_values.png')
plt.close()

# 2. Data Type Distribution
type_counts = results['data_type'].value_counts()
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.barplot(x=type_counts.index, y=type_counts.values)
plt.title('Column Data Type Distribution')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.savefig('data_type_distribution.png')
plt.close()

# 3. Top Frequent Values
categorical_cols = results[results['data_type'].str.contains('categorical')]
top_values_list = []

for c in categorical_cols.index:
    try:
        top_values = parse_top_values(results.loc[c, 'top_values'])
        if not top_values.empty:
            top_values_list.append(top_values)
    except:
        continue

if top_values_list:
    top_values_combined = pd.concat(top_values_list).value_counts().head(20)
    
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    sns.barplot(x=top_values_combined.values, y=top_values_combined.index)
    plt.title('Top 20 Most Frequent Values Across Categorical Columns')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig('top_frequent_values.png')
    plt.close()
else:
    print("No valid top values to plot")

# 4. Numeric Column Distributions
numeric_cols = results[results['data_type'].str.contains('numeric')]
sample_numeric = numeric_cols.sample(5).index

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
for i, col in enumerate(sample_numeric, 1):
    plt.subplot(2, 3, i)
    try:
        data = pd.read_sql(f"SELECT {col} FROM quickbooks__customer_analytics", conn)[col]
        sns.histplot(data.dropna(), kde=True)
        plt.title(col)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error plotting {col}: {str(e)}")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('numeric_distributions.png')
plt.close()

# Generate summary report
summary_stats = {
    'total_columns': len(results),
    'columns_with_missing_values': sum(results['missing_values'] > 0),
    'columns_with_outliers': sum(results['iqr_outliers'].notna()),
    'most_common_data_type': results['data_type'].mode()[0],
    'most_missing_column': results.loc[results['missing_values'].idxmax(), 'data_type']
}

with open('analysis_summary.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write("Data Profiling Summary Report\n")
    f.write("="*40 + "\n")
    f.write(f"Total Columns Analyzed: {summary_stats['total_columns']}\n")
    f.write(f"Columns with Missing Values: {summary_stats['columns_with_missing_values']}\n")
    f.write(f"Columns with Outliers Detected: {summary_stats['columns_with_missing_values']}\n")
    f.write(f"Most Common Data Type: {summary_stats['most_common_data_type']}\n")
    f.write(f"Column with Most Missing Values: {summary_stats['most_missing_column']}\n")
    f.write("\nVisualizations saved as:\n")
    f.write("- missing_values.png\n")
    f.write("- data_type_distribution.png\n")
    f.write("- top_frequent_values.png\n")
    f.write("- numeric_distributions.png\n")

conn.close()
